Q: Create an XML file with multiple XMLNS and multiple nesting in SQL A:

To put attributes into that root node, you need to make FOR XML PATH('Root').

Also you can nest elements by using /. And you don't need to redeclare all the namespaces, instead just put it into your WITH XMLNAMESPACES and use an alias such as t1: on the relevant elements.

WITH XMLNameSpaces (
  Default 'http://www.root.com.au/2013/xml',
  'http://www.root.com.au/2013/xml/Tier1' AS t1
)
SELECT
    GETDATE() AS "@generated",
    'TypeName' AS "@fileType",
    '1.0.1' AS "@schemaVersion",
    t.result1 AS "Tier1/@element1",
    t.date AS "Tier1/@date",
    t.id AS "Tier1/@ID",
    1 AS "Tier1/t1:Tier2/t1:Tier3/Tier4/@Number",
    1 AS "Tier1/t1:Tier2/t1:Tier3/Tier4/@Version"
FROM
    dbo.[table] t
WHERE
    t.id = @pID
FOR XML PATH('Root');

If the root is truly a root, and you have multiple Tier1 rows then you need to nest it. Note the lack of a column alias on the nested value.

WITH XMLNameSpaces (
  Default 'http://www.root.com.au/2013/xml',
  'http://www.root.com.au/2013/xml/Tier1' AS t1
)
SELECT
    GETDATE() AS "@generated",
    'TypeName' AS "@fileType",
    '1.0.1' AS "@schemaVersion",
    (
        SELECT
            t.result1 AS "@element1",
            t.date AS "@date",
            t.id AS "Tier1/@ID",
            1 AS "t1:Tier2/t1:Tier3/Tier4/@Number",
            1 AS "t1:Tier2/t1:Tier3/Tier4/@Version"
        FROM
            dbo.[table] t
        WHERE
            t.id = @pID
        FOR XML PATH('Tier1'), TYPE
    )
FOR XML PATH('Root');

Q: Chaining programmatic expression functions failing in with_columns A:

If you have multiple generators in the same context, you need to unpack them yourself

def my_generator():
    for i in range(3):
        yield pl.lit(i).alias(str(i))

def my_other_generator():
    for i in range(3, 6):
        yield pl.lit(i).alias(str(i))

df = pl.DataFrame({"a": "b"})

df.with_columns(my_generator()) # one genearator works (Polars will consume it)
df.with_columns(*my_generator()) # you can also unpack the generator yourself

# Two generators doesn't work
# TypeError cannot create expression literal for value of type generator.
df.with_columns(my_generator(), my_other_generator())

# solution: you need to unpack them yourself when there is more than one generator
df.with_columns(*my_generator(), *my_other_generator())

Q: Where does python handle modular calculations differently? A:

If you want to use modular arithmetic to perform division by 2, why not use the modular inverse of 2 modulo 63799, i.e. pow(2, -1, 63799) == (63799 + 1) // 2 == 31900, instead of 63799 // 2 == 31899:

n = 63799
inv2 = pow(2, -1, n)  # 31900
db = []
d = 977
db.append(d)
for i in range(5):
    d &= -2  # minus 1 from `d` if `d` is odd, to make the division a floor division
    d = (d * inv2) % n
    db.append(d)

print(db)  # [977, 488, 244, 122, 61, 30]

Note that d &= -2 is necssary for your case, because modular division by 2 is not the same as integer floor division. E.g.:

(977 * 31900) % 63799 == 32388
(32388 * 2) % 63799 == 977
977 // 2 == 488
488 * 2 == 976 != 977
